Q: How does InkDes convert React components into email safe HTML, and why does the output break in email clients? A:

InkDes takes your React components and turns them into an HTML table with inline CSS. That’s the one format every email client understands. Still, don’t expect flawless results some email clients, like Gmail and Outlook, don’t follow all the CSS rules, or sometimes ignore them completely.

  • Good docs to read:

    MJML docs: best reference for email-safe patterns

    React Email docs: similar approach to InkDes

    Litmus blog/guides: real client quirks explained

Q: Does WPA Supplicant have built-in X.509 certificate generation? A:

Proper certificate handling is the role of a PKI (public key infrastructure) and involves much more than just certificate generation - but the whole certificate lifecycle of generation, expiration, revocation, renewal, distribution, ... . It would not make much sense to implement such complex functionality for the use of WPA supplicant only, especially since both free and commercial PKI solutions already exist.

If you just want to create a self-signed certificate use tools like openssl, which is commonly installed on systems running WPA supplicant. There are many instructions available online on how to do it.

Q: Javascript to change asp:textbox visible property to true A:

Control id on server side is not the same in client side. To be the same and to can use ID with javascript you must add to your server controls ClientIDMode="Static"

As example:

<asp:DropDownList ID="ddlDays" ClientIDMode="Static" CssClass="txt_drpbx" runat="server" onchange="ShowHide();">
